lines.text: Many learners say: I stand up at six every day.
Better: I get up at six every day.
Get up means leave your bed.
Get up! I get up at six every day.

data.wrong: I stand up at six every day.
data.right: I get up at six every day.
data.why: Get up means leave your bed.

native.tip: Im Deutschen heißt „aufstehen“ auch „aus dem Bett kommen“. Im Englischen sagen Sie dafür „get up“.

en.tip: German “aufstehen” also means leaving your bed. In English you say “get up” for that.
en.caption: “Aufstehen” from bed is “get up”! Wrong: “I stand up at six every day.” Right: “I get up at six every day.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
